title: Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage — Cost-of-Care Reduction on a Closed Notice-Billed Month
content:
Once a calendar month billed on the County Assistance Office notice has closed, the business office reviews that month's actual charge against the month's cost of care. This review belongs to Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage and concerns the patient pay charge billed for that month from the notice (charge basis "actual notice").

## Governing clauses

- Patient pay never exceeds the month's cost of care.
- For an actual-billed month that the actual-month review prices, a reconciled estimate month that the estimate reconciliation prices and a pending estimate month that the pending-month review prices, the month's cost of care is the cost of care that review's own pricing gives, and only for such a month; every other month remains under the base rule, where the month's cost of care is the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate.
- A month of admission, discharge or death stays under the partial-month rule, by which in a month of admission, discharge or death, patient pay is the lesser of the monthly patient pay and the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, with charge basis "partial month", and any amount already billed above that is reduced with reason `cost_of_care_cap`.
- The reduction the review arrives at is posted against that month's notice charge with reason `cost_of_care_cap`. A charge is reduced once per adjustment reason.

## The posting tool

**What it does.** `post_cost_of_care_reduction_89ef8a19` posts a reduction against one patient pay charge billed on the County Assistance Office notice on a Medical Assistance case: it lowers what the named charge asks of the resident by the amount given and records the reduction, with the reason given, on the case's billing record for the same service month as the charge. The case's patient pay balance falls by the same amount, so a charge that was already paid leaves a credit the resident or representative can see on the case.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `post_cost_of_care_reduction_89ef8a19` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `medicaid_case_id` | the reference number of the resident's Medical Assistance case whose charge is reduced, as returned by the case lookup | identifier |
| `charge_entry_id` | the reference number of the patient pay charge being reduced, as returned by the case billing-record lookup for that case | identifier |
| `adjustment_reason` | the controlled reason recorded on the reduction | one of the five values below |
| `amount` | the reduction in US dollars | a positive number with 2 decimal places (cents), rounded half up to the cent; no currency symbol and no thousands separator |

The values of `adjustment_reason`:

- `trueup_decrease` — an estimate billed during the pending period is lowered to the month's reconciled actual patient pay;
- `patient_pay_redetermined` — a charge is lowered because a County Assistance Office redetermination set a lower patient pay for that month;
- `not_eligible_month` — an estimate for a month outside the eligibility period is taken off;
- `cost_of_care_cap` — a month's patient pay is lowered to the month's cost of care;
- `billing_error` — a charge billed in a wrong amount is corrected.

**Return.** The call is complete when a receipt comes back with status posted. The receipt carries `entry_id` (reference number of the new reduction entry), `medicaid_case_id`, `charge_entry_id`, `service_month` (the charge's service month, YYYY-MM), `adjustment_reason`, `amount` (US dollars with two decimals), `entry_date` (the posting date, YYYY-MM-DD), `patient_pay_balance` (the case's patient pay balance with the reduction posted, two decimals; a leading minus sign means a credit) and status. An amount that is not a positive figure is refused with an error and nothing is recorded.

*Hypothetical receipt reading:* a receipt showing a patient pay balance of "-84.10" means the case now carries a credit of 84.10 dollars.
